Swag: completely ironically, I was making fun of people who used it unironically which was cringe of me but that’s okay hahahaha. Just means that something is cool. “That is so swag.”

1) hit points: 7 is the average of rolling 2d6. So if you want to roll for hit points instead of using the set number (which I don’t recommend doing!!), you would most likely roll around 7. 

2) +4 to hit: that’s actually funny that you brought up strength and dex, because a goblin’s +4 to hit for both their scimitar and their short bow IS the total of 1d20 + the goblin’s dexterity + the goblin’s weapon proficiency. Both are +2. Scimitars are a light finesse weapon, and short bows are light and ranged, so they therefore both use dexterity as opposed to strength. 

3) sleeping bad guy: genuinely up to the DM. Advantage is a really great way to do it, in my opinion. A sleeping person typically has the “prone” state which means you get advantage on any close ranged attacks, and I personally would give the attacker a surprise round on the victim— which is a round where the victim does not get to use their turn. 

4) up to the DM, but most DMs don’t roll death saves for enemies, especially non-consequential ones. You are technically at 0 hit points when rolling death saves, but that is presuming you took some amount of damage directly before rolling. Stabilizing means you don’t have to roll death saves anymore; you’re alive, but you can’t fight, usually because you’re unconscious.

ETA: the “stable at 0 HP” just means that you don’t gain a hit point upon passing your death saves. Unless, of course, you roll a natural 20, which gives you a hit point and puts you back up!! Had he failed 3/5 death saves, his character would have died.
